description: The eight sibling scripts the weekly dogfood runs against, with the fixed inputs in this directory. Paths are relative to the corpus root (env PYSC_REAL_CORPUS, default ~/Documents/prjcts/_own).

cases.name: binary_size
cases.note: Hashes two binaries and parses two Mach-O section reports; 100 percent island.

port.note: The port takes the same argument list as the original, and the three runners share a four and five MiB pair rather than the one and 1.25 MiB pair above: on the small pair the comparison is dominated by CPython's interpreter startup and module imports (35.8 ms against the standalone binary's 3.1 ms), so the larger pair makes the hashing work dominate the native side.

cases.name: classify
cases.note: Regex scan of a 4500 line Wine launch log; 100 percent island.

port.note: The native port raises RuntimeError: regular expression fuel exhausted on the full 4512 line log (divergence 4, 2M steps per search), so the three runners share a 3200 line prefix that keeps every signature and its evidence line. The floor measurement above still uses the full log.

cases.name: tool_token_analysis
cases.note: Reads six synthetic session files from HOME/.maki/sessions and prints the tables; native module top level, all functions island.

cases.name: check_deploy_secrets
cases.note: Loads the secrets manifest with pyyaml and checks twelve names; needs PYSC_REAL_PYYAML pointing at a site-packages with pyyaml.

cases.name: split
cases.note: Startup only: the compiled binary loses process argv when the module top level stays native (#635), so both sides run the argparse usage error.

cases.name: parse_tickets
cases.note: Startup only: the exercise script's main is unfinished (it reads an undefined `lines`), so its only real path is the missing-argument error.

cases.name: caveman_cli
cases.note: Startup only: relative imports mean both interpreters fail with the same ImportError when it is run as a script.

cases.name: validate
cases.exclude: orchestrator: main runs git, uv lock and the per-project gates as subprocesses, so timing it would measure the host toolchain and would put several test suites on a shared machine
